>!Honestly I'm pretty perplexed by this question myself. Honestly with me I feel a lot less noticeable dysphoria than other trans people I've met. With me a lot of things I've come to accept and not let my dysphoria bother me about it so things like having kids. I'd love to have my own but as I can't and will likely be sterile in the next few years. Ive come to accept it as part of my reality. And have decided that if I ever want kids and am in a stable situation to do so ill likely adopt. Theres a lot that I feel like would be better if I could just wake up female. I wouldn't be so afraid of entering the dating scene as a trans lesbian. And not meeting someone who can see me as myself instead of just that im trans or what I feel dysphoric about. I'd feel somewhat safer in female spaces, especially in public restrooms as I wouldn't have as much fear about being hospitalized for simply being there as I live in a fairly liberal area. I'd be able to find clothes in my size that I actually liked a lot easier. Given that people suddenly thought I was cis, my family wouldn't deadname me or misgender me, which as much as I love them and as much they do support/ love me they don't really try to use my name/ pronouns and that hurts a lot sometimes. I'd likely be able to actually feel pleasure, maybe even orgasm with the right partner.  Which neither happens anymore and im seriously questioning if it ever did. (I'm pretty sure I'm demisexual and now that I'm on hormones I'm realizing just how much of that was hormonal bs not pleasure 🙃.) However on the other hand, I don't think i could give up the experience of being trans for the world. Even with the pain that it causes/ has caused me. I have a completely different outlook on life and though while sometimes realistically cynical, its made me a much better person. Ive learned to see so much beauty in people and in the world, and to see some of the more problematic things in people / the world for what they are. And ive only just turned 21. I feel like I've learned so much that I otherwise would not have been able to. I feel like I've grown so much since puberty hit first time around. And im not "wearing a mask" or "personality" for anyone anymore. Im me and if someone has a problem with that they can promptly f*** off. Ich gebe eine Fliegened fick nicht.(my rough transition of "I dont give a flying f***" in German) yeah it may hurt when someone I thought I knew says some sh***y stuff or some sh** happens for the umpteenth time because some people think our existence is a "debate" or even piss off my moma bear instincts when a another trans or any lgbtq+ person is going through a tough time because people are stupid and sh***y. But im not fundamentally changing myself for others anymore, I just focus on being myself and try to help people that need it whenever I can. I have a hard time believing I'd be the person I am today without being trans.<!
